review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with SmallHom.lean, where the corresponding simp lemmas live. I also grepped for uses of the lemmas. Other candidates looked fine. SmallShiftedHom.equiv_comp and equiv_shift are not @[simp], but their SmallHom counterparts (SmallHom.equiv_comp) are not simp either, and call sites invoke them explicitly. The @[simp] lemmas mk₀_comp_mk₀Inv, comp_mk₀_id and mk₀_id_comp have variable LHS patterns and terminate. The only concrete gap I found is the missing @[simp] on smallShiftedHomMap_mk₀. I did not run Lean, so any claim about simp behaviour is inferred from reading the source.

findings.problem: The neighbouring lemma `smallShiftedHomMap_mk` is `@[simp]`, but `smallShiftedHomMap_mk₀` is not, and `mk₀` is not a simp-unfolded definition. `Φ.smallShiftedHomMap eX eY (mk₀ ..)` therefore has no simp rule and `simp` leaves it stuck. The analogous lemma for SmallHom, `smallHomMap'_mk`, is `@[simp]`. The only downstream use, in Ext/Map.lean, has to call it by an explicit `rw` with all arguments supplied. The lemma's own proof is `simp [SmallShiftedHom.mk₀]`, which shows the intended normal form is reachable by rewriting. Its LHS is a head symbol applied to constructor-like `mk₀`, and its RHS is another `mk₀` with no `smallShiftedHomMap`, so it cannot loop.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`, as `smallShiftedHomMap_mk` and `smallHomMap'_mk` are. Under `@[simp]` the `by simp [SmallShiftedHom.mk₀]` proof may become circular or need an `unfold`. If so, prove it with `simp only [SmallShiftedHom.mk₀, smallShiftedHomMap_mk, ...]` or by `rw`. Then drop the explicit `rw [... smallShiftedHomMap_mk₀ ...]` in `Abelian.Ext.mapExactFunctor_mk₀` in favour of `simp`.
findings.benefit: Simp can push `smallShiftedHomMap` through degree-zero morphisms (`mk₀`) the same way it already does for `mk` and for SmallHom. Users then get the normal form `mk₀ (eX.inv ≫ Φ.functor.map f ≫ eY.hom)` without naming the lemma and its explicit arguments.
